reviews.comment: Professor Walters is a great professor. She cares about the students at a professional and personal level. She prioritized all her students having internships during the summer and constantly gave us more reasons to like and respect our major. She is the most passionate professor this department has had.

Professor Walters is extremely passionate about AREN and wants her students to do well in class and outside of class. Her lectures are long and filled with ALOT of information, but she really is helpful if you just ask. People like to complain, but her class is not meant to be difficult. Her outfits always eat too.

She is very passionate and cares for all of of students. Yes she has long boring lectures and her content can be confusing, but she very sweet and wants to see her students succeed. All of these negative comments are just people who complain all the time. Professor Walter's deserves so much better.

Holds you late after class because she showed up late and rambled on about her personal accomplishments. Keep a running counter of how many times she says "sustainability". She's the only prof for this class. The actual class isn't that hard but it is pointless. The entire semester of "content" could be summed up in a 15 minute powerpoint.
reviews.ratingTags: Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Holy yap session, she says so much to mean nothing. I have never been so overwhelmed by nothingness. She talks the whole time and its usually about herself or shoving sustainability down your throat. This class is a waste of money and if it weren't for the fact that it was mandatory I wouldn't have gone at all.
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I don't know what people expect from these classes. AREN 200 is a broad, intro class to the major. Professor Walters tends to ramble, and the lectures don't really build on one another. However, the purpose of AREN 200 is to learn about the field and meet other people in your class, and Professor Walters does a great job of meeting those goals.
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Walters has mastered the concept of "doing too much." She has little substance to discuss in this course other than "sustainability," and clearly wishes every one of her students were on the mechanical track so all of us could create her green buildings forever and ever. Highly frustrating professor, but a necessary evil in this major.
reviews.ratingTags: Group projects--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: While Prof Walters is an extremely charismatic lady who speaks with conviction and passion, the topics she lectures on are wildly boring and uninteresting. It is very evident they kind of have to stretch to justify the major's existence. Bring a book or homework to class and sit somewhere out of sight so you don't feel as bad working during lecture

Professor Walters cares a lot about her students and Architectural Engineering, but that is the end of the positives. The negatives include: no clear grading criteria, a extremely disorganized canvas, the content presented in the course has no clear direction, not getting grades back, and she gave us 1 month to complete a semester long project.
